prompt: I'm starting a brand new Sanity project for a company shipping in en-US, de-DE, fr-FR and ja-JP. They want AI translation that respects their terminology, with an editor approving before anything goes live. Tell me what to put in place and in what order.

rubric.c: Names the locale set as content (l10n.locale documents) rather than configuration
Puts infrastructure and schema deploys before the workflow definition deploy, and explains why order matters
Covers the two datasets: content and the engine's own
Tells the reader to author glossary and style-guide content, not only to install code
Ends with a concrete way to verify the pipeline ran end to end

prompt: New project. Some types are full articles that need translating whole; others are author profiles where only a bio and two SEO fields need translating. How do I set each one up?

rubric.c: Distinguishes the document tier from the field tier by where a translation is stored
Registers each tier in the right place: localizedSchemaTypes versus the static FIELD_TIER registry
Says both tiers run the same workflow definitions
Warns that the choice is a storage shape and is expensive to reverse
Mentions ancestor containers for nested field paths, or the published start perspective

prompt: We have a live Studio with 4,000 articles. Roughly half were translated by hand into de-DE and fr-FR, tracked with a `lang` string field we invented and a boolean `needsRetranslation`. There is also a nightly cron job that calls a translation API. Give me the adoption plan, including the risks.

rubric.c: Says the existing orchestration has to be removed, not run alongside, and explains the concrete failure of keeping both
Addresses migrating the home-grown language field and producing the join documents
Names publishing as the trigger and the workflow instance as the status, replacing the boolean flag
Raises review ownership as an adoption risk, not only technical steps
Does not propose writing custom sync, polling or status-reconciliation code

prompt: Existing setup works for `article`. I need `landingPage` localized too. What do I change?

rubric.c: Lists every place the type name has to appear, not just the Studio config
Includes the workflow definition's subject types and the Function event filters
Says both the blueprint and the definitions must be redeployed
Notes that a missing registration fails differently at each layer rather than loudly

prompt: The shipped definitions don't cover what we need: a compliance sign-off stage for de-DE only, after the machine draft and before publish, with a named approver recorded. I want to build my own workflow. Walk me through it.

rubric.c: Orders the work as definition, bench proof, handler, then deploy — bench before deploy is explicit
Says state belongs on the workflow instance, not on the content document
Covers all the registrations a new definition needs: deploy set, handler map, trigger
Explains that actions are guarded predicates rather than an ordered sequence
Points at a specific existing definition or spec to model the work on

prompt: I need an effect handler that calls our external MT vendor instead of Agent Actions, and writes the result to the target document. What's the contract, and what will bite me?

rubric.c: Names the handler signature and where the shared plumbing is exported from
Puts the idempotency read first and explains at-least-once delivery in terms of cost
Warns that the engine client addresses the workflows dataset only, so content traffic must be routed
Covers narrowing untyped effect params rather than casting them
Keeps the handler free of React and Studio imports, with the reason

prompt: How do I test a workflow definition before it goes anywhere near a real project or an AI credit?

rubric.c: Says the bench runs the real engine in memory with a deterministic clock, no project and no network
Gives the actual entry points used to drive an instance on the bench
Advises asserting on invariants rather than on an exact action transcript
Names the command that runs the suite

prompt: I published an en-US article twenty minutes ago and nothing has happened. No translations, no run visible anywhere. Help me find the problem.

rubric.c: Gives an ordered diagnosis that eliminates one layer at a time rather than a list of guesses
Checks whether the instance exists at all before blaming translation
Names the dataset-and-tag mismatch as a silent failure mode
Checks the deployed definition against the in-code one
States that a run sitting in review is not stuck

prompt: One locale came back empty and the run carried on into review with the others. How do I retry just that locale, and what are the likely causes of the empty result?

rubric.c: Gives the command that re-runs a failed activity
Names schema deployment as a first-order cause of an empty or rejected translation
Covers the assembled style guide exceeding its size budget, and how to reduce it
Explains that one failed locale settling rather than hanging the document run is deliberate

prompt: An editor says publish and schedule are both greyed out on an article and she is stuck. What's going on and what should she do?

rubric.c: Identifies an open run holding a guard on the subject as the cause
Gives the editor real options: finish, request changes, or abort
Explains why schedule needs its own wrapper on top of the workflow plugin's locks
Does not suggest removing or unwrapping the guard

prompt: I have a 300-term termbase exported from our old TMS. Do I load all of it? And how do I know whether any of it is actually helping?

rubric.c: Says no: entries earn their place, and explains which kinds of term produce a measurable difference
Explains content-aware filtering so a whole glossary is never injected into one prompt
Points at with-context versus without-context measurement rather than asserting the benefit
Names do-not-translate entries becoming the API's protected phrases as a harder guarantee than an instruction
Notes which guardrail entries are always kept regardless of filtering

prompt: New to this team. Walk me through what actually happens between an editor pressing publish on an en-US article and a German version being live. I keep hearing instance, effect and drain and I don't know what owns what.

rubric.c: Traces the phases in order from publish through analysis, fan-out, translation, review and publish
Attributes fan-out, retries, gating and idempotency to the engine rather than to repo code
Closes the loop: reviewer corrections become draft proposals that a human must accept and publish
Explains that the engine has no daemon and Sanity Functions are its runtime
Explains stale analysis deciding which locales need work before any AI spend

prompt: Person documents show as not covered for es-ES even though the bio has Spanish text in it. What am I missing?

rubric.c: Says coverage is all-or-nothing across every registered field for that type
Tells the reader to check the other registered fields, naming them, rather than the one they looked at
Names the static registry as the place field paths are declared, and why it is static
Mentions ancestor containers or unregistered paths as adjacent causes

prompt: We're on Astro, not Next. I want locale-prefixed routes, a switcher, and the fallback behaviour your reference Next app has. What maps onto what, and what should I be careful about?

rubric.c: Maps the four framework concerns: client, public env prefix, locale route, server-side fetch and redirect
Insists the locale list is queried from l10n.locale documents rather than hardcoded
Describes the fallback decision as explicit and visible to the reader
Keeps the frontend read-only and free of Studio imports

prompt: If an article isn't translated into pt-BR yet, what should /pt-BR/that-article render? Right now we 404 and marketing is unhappy.

rubric.c: Gives the fallback decision as an ordered rule ending in a 404 only when the source is missing too
Requires the fallback to be visible to the reader rather than silent, and says why
Points at the reference implementation of the decision
Mentions the fallback reference chain on the locale document, and that the reference is single-hop
